To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) blockchain technology is a suitable solution for the management of data in a decentralized environment where the trust is a crucial issue; ii) it can be used to implement a wide range of applications, including those that are not related to the financial field; iii) the most appropriate blockchain category depends on the specific application; and iv) the configuration process is a crucial phase that must be carefully addressed to obtain the expected benefits.

(i) blockchain can be a proper solution for many real-world scenarios, but it is not a silver bullet, (ii) there are three main categories of blockchain, each one suitable for a particular set of problems, and (iii) the blockchain configuration is a crucial aspect, and a wrong choice of it may result in a system that does not fulfill its requirements.
blockchain is not a panacean technology, that it can bring added-value to a wide range of problems, and that its selection and configuration must be driven by a proper requirements analysis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, given a specific business problem and its requirements, the methodology can be used to determine whether a blockchain solution is appropriate and if so, which category of blockchain to use, and how to configure it.

blockchain is a proper technology to be used when: (i) the data is not owned by one entity and is distributed across several entities; (ii) the data is sensitive and its integrity is crucial; (iii) the data must be shared with a limited number of entities; and (iv) the data must have a high level of consistency.
blockchain is not the panacea, and it is important to carefully assess its applicability and configuration before adopting it.

, in order to select the proper blockchain, it is not enough to consider its technical characteristics, but also the problem requirements.
